risks.note: Extensive regulation around sugarcane pricing, export policies, monthly release quotas, and the Minimum Selling Price of sugar exposes profitability to uncontrollable government policy shifts; mitigated via operational excellence and diversification of revenue streams.

Government controls feedstock usage and ethanol pricing (e.g. mandated grain-ethanol mix, FCI rice allocation); mitigated via flexibility in feedstock/product mix and forward integration into IMIL and IMFL capacity.

risks.risk: Demand risk in engineering businesses (PTB and Water)
risks.note: Economic slowdown results in lower capital investment by customers, reducing product demand; mitigated via PTB's diversification across industries/geographies and a strong order book, and Water Business's reliance on government-authority demand.

Gaps in product quality, design, or cost competitiveness can erode market share; mitigated via continuous technology upgrades and new product development (including for defence) while retaining a low-cost advantage.

Long EPC cycles of 2-4 years expose the Water Business to execution delays and customer payment defaults; mitigated via rigorous customer due diligence, diversification through international and PPP projects, and financial closure checks.

Climate change and pest infestations (e.g. spread of red rot in the Co 0238 cane variety) affect sugarcane feedstock availability and quality, directly impacting crush volumes and recovery; mitigated via farmer education programs, crop monitoring, disease prevention and development of resilient cane varieties.

Low domestic sugar prices can adversely impact financial performance given the segment's weight in the business; mitigated via focus on premium products (refined and pharma-grade sugar) and institutional clients to command better margins.

High working capital needs for inventory (sugar, alcohol, grain) and cane payments create funding and liquidity pressure, especially when cane prices or inventories rise; mitigated via efficient cash flow planning, access to credit lines, and strong credit ratings (ICRA A1+ and AA+ with stable outlook).

- **PTB margin:** ~35% PBIT maintained, "same trend expected to continue" post-demerger.

- **Working capital:** short-term borrowings to fall rapidly from April → near-zero by Sep/Oct.
order book & pipeline:
- **Gears/PTB:** order book just under ₹500 cr (+25% YoY); enquiry book "even more robust", "massively skewed" to exports. Landmark Q4 order: **axial-compressor test gearbox** for a premier defence establishment — first-of-its-kind in Asia, full test-rig scope (electricals + mechanicals); supports indigenous gas-engine development, cuts reliance on foreign test facilities. Qualification orders for pumps & compressors (oil & gas / API compliance) under commissioning.
- **Defence:** orders currently double-digit-to-triple-digit ₹cr, delivery 1–4 yrs; many *repeatable* (Navy can re-assign without fresh tender). Not yet into 10-year-programme orders — "well on the way". Success so far with Indian Navy (marine/mechanical); Army & Navy expansion flagged as a possible breakthrough this year.
- **Water:** order book >₹1,500 cr (O&M ₹1,077 cr); FY26 inflow ₹165 cr; completed Exim-Bank-funded Maldives water/sanitation project (6 islands).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Sugar:** crush 8.25 MT (-8.8%, agro-climatic + Gur/Khandsari cane diversion, West-UP crush -17%); recovery 11.06% (+26 bps) on C-heavy molasses; domestic sales 9.79 lakh t (+10.4%) at ₹40,680/t; inventory ~60 lakh quintals valued ₹38.1/kg; current ex-mill refined ~₹42.20 (sulphitation ~₹0.75–1/kg lower). Khatauli only West-UP unit to cross 200 lakh-quintal crush. Govt mooting Sugarcane Control Order revision + bringing Gur/Khandsari under central ambit.
- **Distillery:** highest-ever production & sales; grain 56% of ethanol (maize fell to ~33% of mix from 44% as ESY tender mandated 40% FCI rice); maize most competitive feedstock (best margin > C-molasses > rice variants); conversion + RM cost both down sharply; branded IMIL a top-5 player in UP.
- **Power Transmission (→TPTL):** high-speed turbo gearboxes; **aftermarket ~40% of FY26 gears (vs historical ~30%+)** — high-margin, mostly *other makers'* gearboxes, 50-yr repair heritage, India delivery 2–3 mo vs global ~12 mo. Defence manufacturing facility launched in Q4 (lathes, deep-hole-drilling, floor-boring); multi-modal facility live in Mysore (propulsion shafting + more); Swiss subsidiary driving export order/enquiry book. Customers/OEMs: Siemens, Mitsubishi, Atlas Copco, Sulzer, BHEL, Triveni Turbine.
- **Water:** EPC + long O&M; ZLD/liquid-discharge norms driving recycle/reuse demand; receivables ~₹125–150 cr of group ~₹500 cr.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Data-centre gas turbines:** medium/small gas turbines & engines paired to US (and global) data centres = "huge area of growth" — Triveni pursuing AVL approvals with those OEMs; successes anticipated "next few quarters".
- **Oil & gas (API):** compressor/pump qualification orders + global AVLs (last 3 yrs "massive" progress) open the API-compliant export market; Middle-East pipeline build-out + refurbishment a multi-year CapEx tailwind for compressor test rigs.
- **Defence/marine:** marine gearboxes for Navy (collaborations planned for this specialised "in-between-speed" gearbox); axial-compressor test-rig franchise extendable to other gearbox streams + global test facilities; Navy DPP new-build/revamp CapEx pipeline.
- **Aftermarket internationalisation:** local agents + eventual Triveni staff abroad; faster delivery + lower price point as USP.
- **Biofuel optionality:** Beyond-E20 / E85, FFVs (Triveni among first-5 buyers of a leading FFV launch), isobutanol diesel, SAF ethanol-to-jet — policy "roots".
- **Sugar/distillery organic growth:** Shamli factory return + distillery (idle since acquisition) restart + de-bottlenecking — no greenfield CapEx needed; variety-238 replacement lifts yields.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Consol EBITDA margin 16.9% (up). Distillery turnaround is the swing: lower maize/grain RM + conversion cost down (after by-product credit). Sugar margins held vs +₹300/t cane price via better recovery + cost optimisation + ₹31 cr export-power-tariff gain.
- Gears PBIT ~35% sustained; FY26 aftermarket mix rising to ~40% cushioned margins despite lower revenue & higher overheads. Rupee depreciation (~₹100/$) seen as a net export tailwind (gears + ethanol exports), though it raises maize-equivalent export pull on feedstock.
- ₹14 cr labour-code exceptional charge the only notable distortion.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Gears CapEx ₹340 cr (3 tranches) → ~₹700 cr output; ₹231 cr done (₹78 cr defence); ~₹109 cr left for Q1/Q2 FY27; **complete by Sep-2026** (only the defence facility slightly behind). Defence + multi-modal (Mysore) + new aftermarket repair bay all coming online.
- Sugar/distillery CapEx is cost-reduction-only currently; organic capacity from Shamli + de-bottlenecking (no greenfield/brownfield yet — gated on favourable policy).
capital allocation:
- Final dividend ₹1.25/sh; strong balance sheet, ICRA AA+ reaffirmed.
- TPTL "armed with sufficient cash flows" to self-fund gears CapEx/OpEx post-demerger.
- Commodity (sugar/distillery) cash flows earmarked for future policy-led greenfield/brownfield expansion.
risks & watch-items:
- **Ethanol policy/tender risk:** South-India court case stalled tenders (only reached R1 vs expected R4); no organic ethanol growth this year; pricing (cane- vs grain-linked) hasn't risen in ~2 yrs; FY27 grain EBITDA depends entirely on next tender's quantum/conditions & maize-vs-rice push (govt leaning to rice).
- **Gears Q4 "blip":** West-Asia geopolitical inactivity + domestic CapEx pause delayed export-gearbox acceptance — recovery hinges on Q1/Q2 FY27 shipping the finished-goods backlog.
- **Sugar agro-climatic:** El Niño / Super El Niño monsoon risk; West-UP cane diversion to Gur/Khandsari; cane-price escalation; reliance on DGFT export quotas.
- **Competition:** RENK building local presence (mgmt downplays win-rate impact); not-yet-complete global AVL coverage limits some markets.
- **Demerger execution:** record-date/listing timeline (~end-Aug) and clean separation of two reporting entities.
- **Working capital:** elevated short-term debt from cane-price-driven inventory (should normalise by Sep/Oct); water-EPC receivables.
management quality / tone: - MD candid and detailed; explicitly refused to dress up the gears quarter ("Q4 was not a good quarter for PTB… it is a blip") and declined to give forward numbers repeatedly (consistent no-guidance discipline on order intake/conversion-cost specifics). Confident, almost promotional, on the demerger inflection and data-centre/defence optionality, but appropriately hedged on AVL timing and sugar-crop uncertainty ("if one had a magic ball"). Strong process transparency on cane-survey methodology and AI/ML/drone crop-prediction investment.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The investable event is **structural, not earnings**: the TPTL demerger isolates a ~35%-PBIT, export-levered, asset-light high-speed-gearbox + defence franchise from the policy-driven sugar/ethanol commodity engine — likely to re-rate separately from end-Aug.
- **Aftermarket (~40% of gears, mostly rivals' gearboxes)** is the quiet moat — India 2–3 mo turnaround vs global ~12 mo, fraction of OEM price yet highly profitable; the new Mysore repair bay deepens it and is the springboard for international agency-led expansion.
- The data-centre angle is real but early: Triveni already supplies gearboxes for the few domestic gas-turbine models and is chasing AVLs with the OEMs feeding US data-centre gas-turbine/engine packages — a genuine picks-and-shovels link if AVLs convert.
- Distillery's FY26 jump is partly a **supply-chain/procurement** win (cheap maize sourced/stored across states) not just policy — but the maize→FCI-rice mandate caps the upside and makes FY27 grain EBITDA a tender-policy bet, not a cost-curve bet.
- The first-in-Asia axial-compressor test gearbox is a franchise seed: management frames it as extendable to other gearbox streams and to global test-facility tenders.

growth verticals / optionality:
- **Data-centre gas turbines:** medium/small gas turbines & engines paired to US (and global) data centres = "huge area of growth" — Triveni pursuing AVL approvals with those OEMs; successes anticipated "next few quarters".
- **Oil & gas (API):** compressor/pump qualification orders + global AVLs (last 3 yrs "massive" progress) open the API-compliant export market; Middle-East pipeline build-out + refurbishment a multi-year CapEx tailwind for compressor test rigs.
- **Defence/marine:** marine gearboxes for Navy (collaborations planned for this specialised "in-between-speed" gearbox); axial-compressor test-rig franchise extendable to other gearbox streams + global test facilities; Navy DPP new-build/revamp CapEx pipeline.

- **Biofuel optionality:** Beyond-E20 / E85, FFVs (Triveni among first-5 buyers of a leading FFV launch), isobutanol diesel, SAF ethanol-to-jet — policy "roots".
- **Sugar/distillery organic growth:** Shamli factory return + distillery (idle since acquisition) restart + de-bottlenecking — no greenfield CapEx needed; variety-238 replacement lifts yields.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Consol EBITDA margin 16.9% (up). Distillery turnaround is the swing: lower maize/grain RM + conversion cost down (after by-product credit). Sugar margins held vs +₹300/t cane price via better recovery + cost optimisation + ₹31 cr export-power-tariff gain.
- Gears PBIT ~35% sustained; FY26 aftermarket mix rising to ~40% cushioned margins despite lower revenue & higher overheads. Rupee depreciation (~₹100/$) seen as a net export tailwind (gears + ethanol exports), though it raises maize-equivalent export pull on feedstock.

capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- Gears CapEx ₹340 cr (3 tranches) → ~₹700 cr output; ₹231 cr done (₹78 cr defence); ~₹109 cr left for Q1/Q2 FY27; **complete by Sep-2026** (only the defence facility slightly behind). Defence + multi-modal (Mysore) + new aftermarket repair bay all coming online.
- Sugar/distillery CapEx is cost-reduction-only currently; organic capacity from Shamli + de-bottlenecking (no greenfield/brownfield yet — gated on favourable policy).
capital allocation:
- Final dividend ₹1.25/sh; strong balance sheet, ICRA AA+ reaffirmed.
- TPTL "armed with sufficient cash flows" to self-fund gears CapEx/OpEx post-demerger.
- Commodity (sugar/distillery) cash flows earmarked for future policy-led greenfield/brownfield expansion.
risks & watch-items:
- **Ethanol policy/tender risk:** South-India court case stalled tenders (only reached R1 vs expected R4); no organic ethanol growth this year; pricing (cane- vs grain-linked) hasn't risen in ~2 yrs; FY27 grain EBITDA depends entirely on next tender's quantum/conditions & maize-vs-rice push (govt leaning to rice).
- **Gears Q4 "blip":** West-Asia geopolitical inactivity + domestic CapEx pause delayed export-gearbox acceptance — recovery hinges on Q1/Q2 FY27 shipping the finished-goods backlog.
- **Sugar agro-climatic:** El Niño / Super El Niño monsoon risk; West-UP cane diversion to Gur/Khandsari; cane-price escalation; reliance on DGFT export quotas.
- **Competition:** RENK building local presence (mgmt downplays win-rate impact); not-yet-complete global AVL coverage limits some markets.
- **Demerger execution:** record-date/listing timeline (~end-Aug) and clean separation of two reporting entities.
- **Working capital:** elevated short-term debt from cane-price-driven inventory (should normalise by Sep/Oct); water-EPC receivables.
management quality / tone: - MD candid and detailed; explicitly refused to dress up the gears quarter ("Q4 was not a good quarter for PTB… it is a blip") and declined to give forward numbers repeatedly (consistent no-guidance discipline on order intake/conversion-cost specifics). Confident, almost promotional, on the demerger inflection and data-centre/defence optionality, but appropriately hedged on AVL timing and sugar-crop uncertainty ("if one had a magic ball"). Strong process transparency on cane-survey methodology and AI/ML/drone crop-prediction investment.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The investable event is **structural, not earnings**: the TPTL demerger isolates a ~35%-PBIT, export-levered, asset-light high-speed-gearbox + defence franchise from the policy-driven sugar/ethanol commodity engine — likely to re-rate separately from end-Aug.
- **Aftermarket (~40% of gears, mostly rivals' gearboxes)** is the quiet moat — India 2–3 mo turnaround vs global ~12 mo, fraction of OEM price yet highly profitable; the new Mysore repair bay deepens it and is the springboard for international agency-led expansion.
- The data-centre angle is real but early: Triveni already supplies gearboxes for the few domestic gas-turbine models and is chasing AVLs with the OEMs feeding US data-centre gas-turbine/engine packages — a genuine picks-and-shovels link if AVLs convert.
- Distillery's FY26 jump is partly a **supply-chain/procurement** win (cheap maize sourced/stored across states) not just policy — but the maize→FCI-rice mandate caps the upside and makes FY27 grain EBITDA a tender-policy bet, not a cost-curve bet.
- The first-in-Asia axial-compressor test gearbox is a franchise seed: management frames it as extendable to other gearbox streams and to global test-facility tenders.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: TEIL is a predominantly B2B (with selective B2C) conglomerate operating sugar mills with co-generation, an alcohol/distillery business supplying ethanol to Oil Marketing Companies and IMIL/IMFL to consumers, a water & wastewater EPC/turnkey and O&M business serving government and industrial clients, and a power transmission business manufacturing high- and low-speed gearboxes including defence products. Sugar and Distillery are the largest segments by turnover (51.38% and 37.83% respectively), with Water (3.52%) and Power Transmission (4.45%) smaller engineering segments. Under a Composite Scheme of Arrangement, Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises Ltd amalgamated with the Company effective April 1, 2025, and the Power Transmission Business will demerge into Triveni Power Transmission Limited effective April 1, 2026.

Landmark Q4 order: **axial-compressor test gearbox** for a premier defence establishment — first-of-its-kind in Asia, full test-rig scope (electricals + mechanicals); supports indigenous gas-engine development, cuts reliance on foreign test facilities. Qualification orders for pumps & compressors (oil & gas / API compliance) under commissioning.
- **Defence:** orders currently double-digit-to-triple-digit ₹cr, delivery 1–4 yrs; many *repeatable* (Navy can re-assign without fresh tender). Not yet into 10-year-programme orders — "well on the way". Success so far with Indian Navy (marine/mechanical); Army & Navy expansion flagged as a possible breakthrough this year.
- **Water:** order book >₹1,500 cr (O&M ₹1,077 cr); FY26 inflow ₹165 cr; completed Exim-Bank-funded Maldives water/sanitation project (6 islands).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **PTB margin:** ~35% PBIT maintained, "same trend expected to continue" post-demerger.
- **PTB exports:** OEM-export share targeted **>50% of original-equipment sales** in the "very near future" (Indian OEMs exporting turbine+gearbox packages + direct supply to global OEMs).
- **Gears CapEx:** total board-approved ₹340 cr in 3 tranches → supports ~₹700 cr output (could be higher); ₹231 cr incurred to 31-Mar-26 (₹78 cr of it defence); ~₹109 cr in Q1+Q2 FY27 (~40% of remaining = defence); **all CapEx complete by Sep-2026** (defence facility a small slip).
- **Demerger / listing:** TEIL shareholder share record date within ~4 weeks; **TPTL listing ~end-Aug 2026**; separate Q1 FY27 board meetings, results & calls for both TEIL and TPTL.
- **Sugar season 2026-27:** national production ~27.8 MMT (Maharashtra +23%, Karnataka +16%, UP -3.4%); closing stock ~4.6–4.8 MMT < opening 5 MMT → constructive pricing. Season start ~2H Oct (early Diwali). El Niño / possible "Super El Niño" a swing factor (Triveni West-UP relatively insulated; risk of early cane maturity if low rainfall).
- **Distillery:** OMC + private-tender allocation pipeline 17.18 cr L (cycle 1); further allocations expected once the South-India court case unblocks tenders; "Beyond E20"/E85, FFV CMVR rules, SAF ethanol-to-jet as multi-year optionality. Maize landed cost ~₹0.75–0.80 lower YoY.
- **Working capital:** short-term borrowings to fall rapidly from April → near-zero by Sep/Oct.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Data-centre gas turbines:** medium/small gas turbines & engines paired to US (and global) data centres = "huge area of growth" — Triveni pursuing AVL approvals with those OEMs; successes anticipated "next few quarters".
- **Oil & gas (API):** compressor/pump qualification orders + global AVLs (last 3 yrs "massive" progress) open the API-compliant export market; Middle-East pipeline build-out + refurbishment a multi-year CapEx tailwind for compressor test rigs.
- **Defence/marine:** marine gearboxes for Navy (collaborations planned for this specialised "in-between-speed" gearbox); axial-compressor test-rig franchise extendable to other gearbox streams + global test facilities; Navy DPP new-build/revamp CapEx pipeline.
- **Aftermarket internationalisation:** local agents + eventual Triveni staff abroad; faster delivery + lower price point as USP.
- **Biofuel optionality:** Beyond-E20 / E85, FFVs (Triveni among first-5 buyers of a leading FFV launch), isobutanol diesel, SAF ethanol-to-jet — policy "roots".
- **Sugar/distillery organic growth:** Shamli factory return + distillery (idle since acquisition) restart + de-bottlenecking — no greenfield CapEx needed; variety-238 replacement lifts yields.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sugar closing stock at 4.2 MMT is the lowest in eight years with only a thin safety buffer before the new crushing season; government shifted sugar from 'restricted' to 'prohibited' export category with a blanket export ban till September 30, 2026, expected to keep domestic sugar prices firm and buoyant
- Global sugar surplus for 2025-26 estimated at ~2.2 MMT by ISO, but 2025-27 could see the surplus flip into a global deficit of ~0.23 MMT on El Nino concerns and a projected 1.1% contraction in global crop
- Water & wastewater treatment market growth: India's market valued at USD 10.4 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 19.4 billion by 2034 (7% CAGR); global market projected to grow from USD 372.39 billion (2025) to USD 713.96 billion by 2034 (7.50% CAGR)
- Water demand driver: Union Budget 2026-27 allocated Rs 2,16,654 crores toward water supply, sanitation and river conservation (JJM Rs 67,670 crores; Namami Gange targeting an additional 600 MLD sewage treatment capacity), alongside stricter enforcement of ZLD norms and the new Liquid Discharge Management Rules 2025 accelerating industrial demand across textiles, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and power sectors
- Distillery: government vision of enhancing ethanol blending beyond 20% (E20), plus emerging bio-isobutanol blending, ethanol stoves and sustainable aviation fuel via the ethanol-to-jet pathway, seen as an expanding demand opportunity given the Company's multi-feedstock capability
- Power Transmission: growing enquiries from both global and domestic customers, proven technical competence and cost efficiencies underpin a sustained growth path; Middle East emerging as a key growth vector and the Swiss step-down subsidiary Triveni Power Transmission GmbH broadening European customer acceptance
- Macro backdrop: Indian economy placed resiliently in a challenging global context, with domestic demand healthy and policy measures supportive of growth in the sectors where the Company operates
- Power Transmission Business ended FY26 with a 25% increase in order book; order booking remained resilient at Rs 467 crores, resulting in an order position of Rs 485 crores as of March 31, 2026, providing strong revenue visibility
- Water Business total order book as of March 31, 2026 stood at Rs 1,503 crores, of which Rs 1,077 crores is towards long-duration O&M contracts, giving multi-year revenue visibility; total order booking during FY26 was Rs 165 crores, including EPC orders of Rs 125.84 crores
- Ethanol: solid allocation pipeline of 17.18 crore litres of ethanol supply tied up under Cycle-1 of the OMC tender and with Private OMCs, with expectation of further allocations in the subsequent cycle; an additional 1.8 crore litres of ENA earmarked for potable alcohol
- Gears business: overall enquiry inflow doubled in the product segment and grew 46% in the aftermarket segment during FY26; 24 high-potential international customers added

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Consol EBITDA margin 16.9% (up). Distillery turnaround is the swing: lower maize/grain RM + conversion cost down (after by-product credit). Sugar margins held vs +₹300/t cane price via better recovery + cost optimisation + ₹31 cr export-power-tariff gain.
- Gears PBIT ~35% sustained; FY26 aftermarket mix rising to ~40% cushioned margins despite lower revenue & higher overheads. Rupee depreciation (~₹100/$) seen as a net export tailwind (gears + ethanol exports), though it raises maize-equivalent export pull on feedstock.
- ₹14 cr labour-code exceptional charge the only notable distortion.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Final dividend ₹1.25/sh; strong balance sheet, ICRA AA+ reaffirmed.
- TPTL "armed with sufficient cash flows" to self-fund gears CapEx/OpEx post-demerger.
- Commodity (sugar/distillery) cash flows earmarked for future policy-led greenfield/brownfield expansion.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Power Transmission Business (PTB): capital expenditure to enhance gears-business capacity (excluding Defence) to Rs 700 crores, with all such capex likely to be completed by September 2026, enhancing revenue potential from Rs 400 crores to Rs 700 crores and positioning the business to address global demand, improve delivery timelines and scale OEM and aftermarket segments. PTB's R&D laboratory development reached the final stage of commissioning during FY26, strengthening in-house testing and validation capability. On the Defence side, key machinery items have been installed and commissioned at PTB's new multi-modal Defence manufacturing facility in Mysuru, alongside commissioning of precision marine shaft manufacturing infrastructure. Sugar/Distillery operations: the Company continued capex on energy conservation and efficiency enhancement across its plants during FY26 - installation of high-efficiency vacuum pans and pan circulators, condensate-based juice heating and waste heat recovery systems, conversion of extraction-condensing turbines to back-pressure turbines, insulation and cooling-system optimisation, and continued deployment of variable frequency drives and LED lighting; this follows a larger FY25 push (new backpressure turbine, VFDs, upgraded utility infrastructure, improved bagasse storage/drainage, flowmeters, condensate-based juice heaters, anaerobic filters). Cane development programmes under the Sugar Business (varietal substitution, climate-resilient agronomic practices) also received continued investment in FY26.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - MD candid and detailed; explicitly refused to dress up the gears quarter ("Q4 was not a good quarter for PTB… it is a blip") and declined to give forward numbers repeatedly (consistent no-guidance discipline on order intake/conversion-cost specifics). Confident, almost promotional, on the demerger inflection and data-centre/defence optionality, but appropriately hedged on AVL timing and sugar-crop uncertainty ("if one had a magic ball"). Strong process transparency on cane-survey methodology and AI/ML/drone crop-prediction investment.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong farmer relations and timely sugarcane payment, with an extensive cane development programme and demo plots across all eight sugar units
- Product-mix focus toward superior-quality sugar (lower ICUMSA, smaller-grain pharma grades, larger-grain sugar) commanding superior realisations
- Diversified alcohol portfolio (Ethanol/ENA/IMIL/IMFL) reducing dependence on a single commodity and buffering the balance sheet
- Power Transmission Business: diversification across industries and geographies, strong order book, continuous technology upgrades retaining a low-cost advantage, and entry into defence products
- Credit ratings of ICRA A1+ (short-term) and AA+ (Stable, long-term) supporting access to credit lines for working capital

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Ethanol policy/tender risk:** South-India court case stalled tenders (only reached R1 vs expected R4); no organic ethanol growth this year; pricing (cane- vs grain-linked) hasn't risen in ~2 yrs; FY27 grain EBITDA depends entirely on next tender's quantum/conditions & maize-vs-rice push (govt leaning to rice).
- **Gears Q4 "blip":** West-Asia geopolitical inactivity + domestic CapEx pause delayed export-gearbox acceptance — recovery hinges on Q1/Q2 FY27 shipping the finished-goods backlog.
- **Sugar agro-climatic:** El Niño / Super El Niño monsoon risk; West-UP cane diversion to Gur/Khandsari; cane-price escalation; reliance on DGFT export quotas.
- **Competition:** RENK building local presence (mgmt downplays win-rate impact); not-yet-complete global AVL coverage limits some markets.
- **Demerger execution:** record-date/listing timeline (~end-Aug) and clean separation of two reporting entities.
- **Working capital:** elevated short-term debt from cane-price-driven inventory (should normalise by Sep/Oct); water-EPC receivables.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The investable event is **structural, not earnings**: the TPTL demerger isolates a ~35%-PBIT, export-levered, asset-light high-speed-gearbox + defence franchise from the policy-driven sugar/ethanol commodity engine — likely to re-rate separately from end-Aug.
- **Aftermarket (~40% of gears, mostly rivals' gearboxes)** is the quiet moat — India 2–3 mo turnaround vs global ~12 mo, fraction of OEM price yet highly profitable; the new Mysore repair bay deepens it and is the springboard for international agency-led expansion.
- The data-centre angle is real but early: Triveni already supplies gearboxes for the few domestic gas-turbine models and is chasing AVLs with the OEMs feeding US data-centre gas-turbine/engine packages — a genuine picks-and-shovels link if AVLs convert.
- Distillery's FY26 jump is partly a **supply-chain/procurement** win (cheap maize sourced/stored across states) not just policy — but the maize→FCI-rice mandate caps the upside and makes FY27 grain EBITDA a tender-policy bet, not a cost-curve bet.
- The first-in-Asia axial-compressor test gearbox is a franchise seed: management frames it as extendable to other gearbox streams and to global test-facility tenders.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Restructuring] The Composite Scheme of Arrangement became effective on 19 May 2026 after NCLT orders of 7 and 18 May 2026: SSEL amalgamated into TEIL with effect from 1 April 2025 and the Power Transmission Business demerged into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd with effect from 1 April 2026.
- [Demerger mechanics] TPTL issued 1 share of Rs 2 for every 3 TEIL shares of Rs 1 held on the 22 July 2026 record date, cutting TEIL's stake in TPTL to 29.88% so TPTL becomes an associate; Rs 445.28 crore of net assets were derecognised, Rs 133.05 crore added to investments and Rs 312.23 crore adjusted against other equity. The demerger rationale cited is PTB's attained size, scale and large growth headroom.
- [Sugar policy/cycle] Closing stock for SS 2025-26 is expected at a 10-year low of 4.10 MMT after 0.70 MMT exports and ~3.00 MMT ethanol diversion; FRP for SS 2026-27 has been raised Rs 10/qtl to Rs 365/qtl, and CACP has suggested exploring dual pricing for household versus commercial users (the latter consuming 60-65% of domestic sugar).
- [Ethanol policy] ESY 2025-26 blending reached 20.0% by June 2026 on 717 crore litres procured, with grain-based ethanol at 66.9% of supply and 72.5% of Cycle 1 allocation; an inter-ministerial group with NITI Aayog is building the 'Beyond E-20' roadmap, SAF blending mandates of 1% by 2027 rising to 5% by 2030 have been set, and CACP has recommended revising cane-based ethanol prices.
- [Shareholding] Promoters hold 60.58% and free float is 39.42% of ~22.04 crore shares of Re 1 each; market capitalisation as on 30 June 2026 was about Rs 9,306 crore.
